source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Data Canopy's Lithia Springs campus publishes 10 MW of IT capacity and 19,500 square feet of technical space, a mid-scale footprint rather than a hyperscale one.

The operator does not publish a rack count, an accelerator count, or a power density, so any conversion is ours, not theirs. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 10 MW of IT load is roughly 250 racks. At a lower 10 kW per rack, the same load is about 1,000 racks. The published square footage does not settle which figure applies, because 19,500 square feet across 250 racks implies about 78 square feet per rack, a plausible hall, while 1,000 racks would imply under 20 square feet per rack, which is tight for training gear.

The only published certification is LEED. That qualifies the building for a green building rating, and it says nothing about power redundancy, cooling topology, or network paths. It does not tell a reader whether the campus can host high-density training racks, and no such specification is published on the page this site read.

In Georgia, this campus ranks third by published megawattage among the five facilities in the state that publish a figure. Those five total 76.3 MW, so this 10 MW campus is about 13 percent of the state's published capacity. The state has 49 mapped facilities, and most of them publish no figure at all, so the published total is a floor rather than a full accounting of Georgia's data center load. For a reader asking whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the answer is that it is a documented, mid-sized load in a state where published capacity is scarce and the grid, not the building, is the constraint.
